Purpose of HLD

The High Level Design Document (HLD) is the single solution document created during a project. It contains solution summary, architectural information and solution details that are used as an input for development and testing activities.

How to Complete this Document
The BSA (or Solution Delivery Manager in the case where the project is without a BSA) is responsible for collating information and populating Business Section (Section 1) of this document
The Solution Architect (SA), with input from the Infra Solution Architect, ICSU and the Enterprise Architect is responsible for completing the Architecture Section (Section 2) of this document
After the completion of Sections 1 and 2, the SA is responsible for submitting the HLD to the DA for approval
Sequel to DA approval, the BSA (Solution Delivery Manager in the case where the project is without a BSA) is responsible for coordinating and consolidating inputs from requisite Tech teams to complete the Technical Section (Section 3) of this document and obtaining sign-offs as required.
This document must be submitted technical and business stakeholder approvals via Jira workflow, leveraging a Jira HLD ticket (see How to Create an HLD Artifact ticket for details).
It is recommended that this document (HLD) be hosted as a shared document on the Project website so updates can be made simultaneously by participating stakeholders

This document consolidates the end‑to‑end business and technical requirements identified. The objective is to provide a clear, agreed‑upon view of what this project must deliver across vendors, platforms, and support teams. [Context: 1.3 Solution Summary] [Focus: ]
1.3 Solution Summary

Amazon Quick Sight is data visualization and analysis component of Amazon Quick. 

Amazon Connect data lake is centralized repository for data generated by Amazon Connect and Amazon Quick Sight is BI tool which will help build dashboard for day2 operation. In short, the amazon connect data lake is single source for all connect data with zero-ETL (i.e no complex data pipeline need to be maintained). This is quickset and fastest way to build dashboard for connect.

The AWS Data export will allow export of CUR 2.0 report to a S3 bucket, which can be visualized using Athena and Amazon Quick Sight. 

In other words, Athena can query data (S3) to create dashboard for Business using Amazon Quick Sight.

Architecture Overview:

This is update to architecture released for CCR release v1.0 [High Level Design - Contact Center Re-Platform - MVP (non-PCI)#2.7.1SolutionArchitectureView]. The key update is integration Amazon Quick Sight to Amazon Connect customer. 



The Amazon Connect Customer Data Lake is AWS created and Managed resource and Amazon Connect Customer uses AWS RAM to shares its data tables to other account / roles / users. S3 (Lex Calls) Bucket Policy

	

This is a tightly scoped resource-based policy attached directly to the S3 bucket.

This policy enforces defense-in-depth security posture via implementing explicit deny-by-default model by:

Denying object read access to all principals except for:
Amazon Lex;
Unconditionally preventing the policy removal, changing Object Lock, or Lifecycle rules by any principal. These actions can only be performed by the account root user.




	
Enable "S3 Block Public Access"


Deny "PUT" to All Except Amazon Connect :

Effect: Deny
Principal: *
Action: s3:PutObject 
Resource: ARN of the the S3 (Lex Calls) bucket and every object in the bucket.
Condition: {"StringNotEquals:{"aws:PrincipalArn":[<ARNs of the Amazon Lex SLR>]}}





Deny "GET" to All Except Amazon Connect:

Effect: Deny
Principal: *
Action: s3:GetObject
Resource: ARN of the the S3 (Lex Calls) bucket and every object in the bucket.
Condition: {"StringNotEquals:{"aws:PrincipalArn":[<ARNs of the Amazon Lex SLR>]}}



Deny Object Lock or Policy Changes to All:

Effect: Deny 
Principal: *
Action: s3:DeleteBucketPolicy, s3:PutObjectRetention, s3:BypassGovernanceRetention, s3:PutBucketObjectLockConfiguration
Resource: ARN of the S3 (Lex Calls) bucket and every object in the bucket.
Condition: {"StringNotEquals:{"aws:PrincipalArn":[<ARN of the Deployer IAM Role>]}} - (see NOTE-1)

 

Deny Lifecyle Config Changes to All (Except Deployer role):

Effect: Deny 
Principal: *
Action: s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration - (see NOTE-2)
Resource: ARN of the S3 (Lex Calls) bucket.
Condition: {"StringNotEquals:{"aws:PrincipalArn":[<ARN of the Deployer IAM Role>]}} - (see NOTE-1)

 

Deny Object Deletion to All (see NOTE-3):

Effect: Deny 
Principal: *
Action: s3:DeleteObject, s3:DeleteObjectVersion
Resource: ARN of the S3 (Lex Calls) bucket.


	

NOTE-1:  In DEV, additional IAM roles (e.g. Developer) may be temporarily added to the Condition exception list in the Deny statement but must be removed before PROD.

NOTE-2: It is not possible to block s3:DeleteLifecycleConfiguration action at the resource-based bucket policy level. This permission is reserved for IAM policy or SCP.

NOTE-3: Lifecycle rules must be enabled and configured to delete each object 1 year after it's been stored.  The lifecycle rule + this "Deny" statement allows to effectively achieve the same data retention policy as ObjectLock. 

S3 Protection is enabled via Amazon GuardDuty (in RCI Centralized Security Center) to detect anomalous data access or unauthorized activity in this bucket.
